newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian children greet freedom at dawn.
newsitem.headline: Indian children greet freedom at dawn.

text.p: Thousands of school children squatting on dusty carpets waved small tricolour paper flags at dawn outside the capital's 17th century Red Fort on Friday to herald India's 50 years of freedom from British rule.

Wearing crisp sashes displaying the colours of India's national flag, the children hummed patriotic songs and cheered Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral as he declared war against corruption and highlighted the plight of girl children.

Amid tight security, Gujral stood behind a bullet-proof glass shield as he addressed the audience of political leaders, ministers, diplomats and children spread in neat lines below the ramparts of the sandstone fort.

Its majestic walls, built by Moghul emperor Shah Jahan, were draped with the saffron, white and green of the national flag. A floral fresco below the podium proclaimed 50 years of India's independence.
Marigolds lined the path to the spectators' seats, and security guards frisked visitors as they arrived.
A giant golden balloon in the shape of India's national emblem hovered over the site in Old Delhi, the city's crowded and bustling centre.

The emblem showed four standing lions back-to-back, three of them visible at a time. At the base were images of a bull and a horse symbolising the movement of life. The emblem was first used by Buddhist Emperor Ashoka more than 2,000 years ago.
India adopted the emblem as a national symbol when it won freedom from British rule in 1947. The wheel in the emblem forms the centre of the flag.
But the balloon collapsed minutes before Gujral unfurled the national flag when four MI-8 helicopters trailing flags flew overhead, showering petals on the gathering.
Before Gujral spoke, three Russian Sukhoi-30 fighter aircraft, the latest acquisition of the Indian Air Force, roared past. One performed a roll as the others peeled off to the sides.
They were followed by eight Indian Air Force trainer jets trailing smoke in the three colours of the national flag.
At the end of the 90-minute celebration, hundreds of coloured balloons were released into the monsoon sky as Gujral and dignitaries quietly left.
